intro: You're looking for a commercial property solicitor near you because you have a business premises issue that needs legal expertise. Whether you're taking on a lease, buying or selling a property, or dealing with a dispute, a local solicitor can help you understand your rights and obligations. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a commercial property solicitor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people searching for a commercial property solicitor near me are facing a business property matter that requires specialist legal advice.
needs: You are about to sign a new lease for business premises and want the terms on repair and rent review checked before you commit.
You are buying or selling a shop, office or industrial unit and need the legal transfer handled properly.
You are dealing with a landlord who is not maintaining the property or is disputing service charges.
You need advice on whether your lease has security of tenure and what happens when it ends.
You are a landlord facing a tenant who has stopped paying rent or is breaching the lease terms.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about commercial property solicitors near you
context: Commercial property solicitors are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) in England and Wales, the Law Society of Scotland in Scotland, and the Law Society of Northern Ireland in Northern Ireland. You can check an individual or firm on the relevant register. Regulated firms must hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure; if that does not resolve things, the Legal Ombudsman can look at service complaints in England and Wales.

The word "lawyer" is not protected on its own, so check that whoever handles your matter is a solicitor, a chartered legal executive (CILEx) or another authorised professional. Reserved activities such as conducting court litigation and certain probate and conveyancing work can only be carried out by authorised people.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: The type of commercial property involved, such as a shop, office, warehouse or development site.
Whether you are buying, selling, leasing, or dealing with a dispute.
If it is a lease, the length of the term and whether security of tenure is being excluded.
Any specific concerns, such as repair obligations, rent review or service charges.
The location of the property so we can introduce you to a solicitor near you.
Any deadlines you are working towards, such as a completion date or lease start date.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the commercial property solicitor
questions: What experience do you have with commercial property matters like mine?
How will you charge for your work, and can you give me an estimate?
What are the key risks in this lease or contract that I should be aware of?
How long do you expect the matter to take?
Will you handle the work yourself or will it be passed to someone else?
What do you need from me to get started?

faqs.q: Do I need a commercial property solicitor to sign a business lease?
faqs.a: It is strongly advisable. A solicitor can check the lease terms, including repair obligations and rent review provisions, and explain your rights and obligations before you commit.

faqs.q: What is security of tenure in a commercial lease?
faqs.a: Security of tenure gives a business tenant the right to renew the lease at the end of the term, unless the landlord has a valid ground to oppose. A solicitor can advise whether it applies to your lease and whether it should be excluded.

faqs.q: Can iComply recommend a commercial property solicitor near me?
faqs.a: iComply introduces you to a suitable UK professional based on your needs. We do not recommend or endorse any particular solicitor, but we can connect you with one who handles commercial property matters.

faqs.q: How do I check that a commercial property solicitor is regulated?
faqs.a: You can check whether a solicitor or firm is regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) in England and Wales, the Law Society of Scotland in Scotland, or the Law Society of Northern Ireland in Northern Ireland. Always ask for the name of the individual handling your matter and verify their status.

extra_heading: What "near me" means when the property is commercial
extra: With commercial property, the solicitor who acts for you does not always need to be on the doorstep of the premises itself. Much of the work is done on paper and by email, so what matters more is that they know the local market and the type of property you are dealing with, whether that is a high street shop, an office or an industrial unit.

A solicitor based near the property can be useful if there is a dispute over repairs, access or a boundary, because they may already know the area and can attend a site visit or a meeting with the other side more easily. For a straightforward lease or purchase, a firm further away that handles commercial property day to day may suit you just as well.

So when you weigh up options, ask each solicitor how they would handle the practical side of your matter, such as who attends meetings and how quickly they can get to the premises if needed. That tells you more about fit than distance alone, and it keeps the decision in your hands rather than relying on a label.

extra_faqs.q: Does my commercial property solicitor need to be based in the same town as the premises?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many commercial property matters are handled remotely, but a local solicitor can be an advantage for site visits, disputes over repairs or access, and meetings with the other side. Ask how they would manage those practicalities before you decide.

extra_faqs.q: What should I bring to the first appointment with a commercial property solicitor?
extra_faqs.a: Bring the draft lease or contract, any correspondence with the landlord or other side, and details of the property such as its address and use. If a deadline is approaching, such as a completion or lease start date, tell them at the outset so the work can be planned around it.

extra_faqs.q: Is a commercial property solicitor the same as a conveyancer?
extra_faqs.a: A solicitor who handles commercial property may do the conveyancing for a business purchase or sale as part of their work, but commercial leases and disputes often need broader advice on terms such as repair, rent review and security of tenure. Ask what share of their work is commercial property so you know they are used to your type of matter.
